Definition: of Hebrew origin (H6005); God with us; Emmanuel, a name of Christ:--Emmanuel.
BiblicalUsage: Emmanuel is the name the angel gives the child born of the virgin in Matthew 1:23, and Matthew pauses to translate it himself: God with us. It is the only place the name stands in the New Testament, and it stands at the very beginning of the story, before Jesus does a single thing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this name is the whole gospel in two words — God did not stay far off, He came to be with us. That is the promise I hold onto when God feels distant: Emmanuel means He already came near.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary
